title: The subsheaf of sections annihilated by a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ put $\mathcal F'(U)=\{s\in\mathcal F(U):\ a\,s|_V=0\text{ for every open }V\subseteq U\text{ and every }a\in\mathcal I(V)\}$. Then $\mathcal F'$ is a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal F$ (the *subsheaf of sections annihilated by* $\mathcal I$), and: (1) $\mathcal F'$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module; (2) for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, $\mathcal F'(U)=\{s\in\mathcal F(U):\ a s=0\text{ for all }a\in\mathcal I(U)\}$; (3) for every $x\in X$, identifying $\mathcal F'_x$ with a submodule of $\mathcal F_x$ and $\mathcal I_x$ with an ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ through the (injective) stalk maps of the inclusions [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], $\mathcal F'_x=\{s\in\mathcal F_x:\ a s=0\text{ for all }a\in\mathcal I_x\}$.

proof.text: For an inclusion of opens $V\subseteq U$, restriction sends a section killed by every local section of $\mathcal I$ to one with the same property on $V$. Sums and $\mathcal O_X$-multiples retain that property. If sections $s_j\in\mathcal F'(U_j)$ agree on overlaps of a covering of $U$, their glued section $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ is killed by every $a\in\mathcal I(V)$: on the cover $V\cap U_j$ each product $a\,s|_V$ vanishes, hence it vanishes on $V$. Thus $\mathcal F'$ is a subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules of $\mathcal F$.

Fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and write $\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde M$ and $\mathcal I|_U\cong\widetilde I$ with $M=\mathcal F(U)$ and $I=\mathcal I(U)\subseteq A$. The finite-type hypothesis gives generators $g_1,\ldots,g_t$ of $I$. On each principal open $D(f)\subseteq U$, the two sheaves have modules of sections $M_f$ and $I_f$. Hence a section $s\in M$ annihilated by $I$ is annihilated by $\mathcal I$ on every $D(f)$, and therefore on every open $V\subseteq U$ by the sheaf condition for $\mathcal F$. Conversely, the defining condition for $\mathcal F'(U)$ applied with $V=U$ says $Is=0$. This proves clause (2), and the same argument on $D(f)$ gives $\mathcal F'(D(f))=\{z\in M_f:I_fz=0\}$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof, affine reduction and proof of (2)

proof.text: Put $M'=\{m\in M:Im=0\}$. For every $f\in A$, localization gives $(M')_f\subseteq\{z\in M_f:I_fz=0\}$. For the reverse inclusion write $z=m/f^n$ and let $g_i$ range over the finitely many generators of $I$. If $g_i z=0$ in $M_f$, there is $e_i\ge0$ with $f^{e_i}g_i m=0$ in $M$. Choose $e$ at least every $e_i$; then $f^e m\in M'$ and $z=(f^e m)/f^{n+e}$ lies in $(M')_f$. The calculation also covers $I=0$ by taking $e=0$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof, localization calculation after 'To show F prime is quasi-coherent'

proof.text: By steps 2 and 3, on every principal open $D(f)\subseteq U$ the submodule $\mathcal F'(D(f))$ is canonically $(M')_f=\widetilde{M'}(D(f))$ inside $M_f$, and these equalities commute with restriction to smaller principal opens. Principal opens form a basis of $U$, so they identify the two sheaves $\mathcal F'|_U\cong\widetilde{M'}$. The latter is quasi-coherent. Since every point has an affine open neighbourhood, $\mathcal F'$ is quasi-coherent on $X$, proving clause (1).

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof, conclusion of (1) from the principal-open calculation

proof.text: Let $x\in U$ correspond to a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and set $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$. Stalk localization identifies $\mathcal F'_x=(M')_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathcal F_x=M_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathcal I_x=I_{\mathfrak p}$, compatibly with the inclusion maps; these maps on stalks are injective. Certainly $(M')_{\mathfrak p}$ is killed by $I_{\mathfrak p}$. Conversely, write $z=m/s\in M_{\mathfrak p}$ with $s\in S$ and suppose $I_{\mathfrak p}z=0$. For each of the finitely many generators $g_i$, the equality $g_i m/s=0$ gives $t_i\in S$ with $t_i g_i m=0$. Put $t=\prod_i t_i\in S$ (and $t=1$ when $I=0$). Then $tm\in M'$ and $z=tm/(ts)$ belongs to $(M')_{\mathfrak p}$. This proves clause (3) including the identification as submodules.
